section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Delaware is known as the 'First State' partly because it was first to ratify the U.S. Constitution. Delaware also had one of the nation's first comprehensive seat belt laws. Which occupants must wear a seatbelt in Delaware today?
options: a:Only the driver,b:Driver and front-seat passengers only,c:All occupants in the vehicle,d:Only passengers under age 18
note: Delaware requires all vehicle occupants — front and rear — to wear a seatbelt. Delaware has primary enforcement, meaning officers can stop a vehicle solely for a seatbelt violation. Delaware's early adoption of comprehensive seatbelt laws reflects its historical role as a legislative pioneer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age to apply for a learner's permit in Delaware?
options: a:14,b:15,c:15 and a half,d:16
note: Delaware requires applicants to be at least 16 years old to apply for a learner's permit. This is older than many states that allow permits at 15 or 15½. After holding the permit for 6 months and meeting supervised driving requirements, they can apply for a Level 2 license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for adult drivers (age 21+) in Delaware?
note: Delaware's per se DUI limit is 0.08% BAC for adult drivers. Commercial drivers face a 0.04% limit. A BAC of 0.08% or higher is sufficient for a DUI charge regardless of apparent impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Delaware's zero tolerance law, the illegal BAC for drivers under 21 is:
note: Delaware sets the underage DUI threshold at 0.02% BAC. A driver under 21 with a BAC at or above 0.02% faces license revocation and criminal penalties. This effectively makes any alcohol consumption illegal before driving for underage drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Delaware's GDL program, how many hours of supervised driving must a Level 1 permit holder complete before applying for a Level 2 license?
options: a:20 hours including 5 at night,b:30 hours including 10 at night,c:40 hours including 10 at night,d:50 hours including 10 at night
note: Delaware requires 50 hours of supervised driving practice, including at least 10 hours at night, before a Level 1 permit holder can apply for a Level 2 restricted license. This practice must be certified by a parent or legal guardian.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on most urban streets in Delaware when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:30 mph,d:35 mph
note: Delaware's default speed limit in urban areas is 25 mph where no limit is posted. Always check for posted signs — many streets have limits that differ from the default, and school zones have even lower limits when active.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Delaware, what does the GDL nighttime restriction require for Level 2 (restricted) license holders under 18?
options: a:No nighttime restriction applies,b:No driving between 10 PM and 6 AM,c:No driving between midnight and 5 AM,d:No driving after 9 PM
note: Delaware Level 2 restricted license holders under 18 may not drive between 10 PM and 6 AM unless accompanied by a licensed adult 25 or older in the front seat, or driving to/from work or school with documentation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when a school bus stops on a two-lane Delaware road and activates its flashing red lights?
options: a:Stop only if driving behind the bus,b:Slow to 15 mph and proceed,c:Stop in both directions at least 20 feet from the bus until lights stop flashing,d:Yield only when children are visible crossing
note: Delaware law requires vehicles in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop arm. You may not proceed until the lights stop flashing and the arm retracts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit in a Delaware school zone when children are present?
options: a:10 mph,b:15 mph,c:20 mph,d:25 mph
note: Delaware school zones have a 20 mph speed limit when children are present or warning lights are active. Slow down well before entering the zone and remain alert for children on or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Delaware highway and see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights. What does the Move Over law require?
options: a:Slow to 25 mph and maintain your lane,b:Move one lane away from the stopped vehicle if safe; if not, slow to a safe speed,c:Stop completely until the vehicle moves,d:Only move over for police — not tow trucks or utility vehicles
note: Delaware's Move Over law requires drivers to vacate the lane adjacent to any stopped emergency, law enforcement, towing, or highway maintenance vehicle with flashing lights. If a lane change is not safe, slow to a speed that is reasonable for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on Delaware interstates?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: Delaware's maximum interstate speed limit is 65 mph. Delaware is a small, densely populated state where traffic is heavy near Wilmington and Dover. Urban sections of interstates are often posted at lower limits — always follow posted signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Delaware, what does a flashing yellow light mean at an intersection?
options: a:Stop completely and yield before proceeding,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:The signal is broken — treat it as a 4-way stop,d:Do not enter the intersection under any circumstances
note: A flashing yellow light is a caution indicator in Delaware. Reduce speed and proceed carefully — a full stop is not required (unlike a flashing red, which requires a complete stop). Scan carefully for crossing vehicles and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane Delaware road, a solid yellow line is on your side of the center. You want to pass the vehicle ahead. You may:
options: a:Pass if you can do so in under 5 seconds,b:Pass only if the other car is going more than 10 mph under the limit,c:Not pass — the solid yellow on your side prohibits crossing the center line,d:Pass only if you first signal for 100 feet
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the road is an absolute prohibition on crossing the center line to pass. Wait for a dashed yellow line on your side before attempting to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Delaware's implied consent law, refusing a chemical test after a DUI stop results in:
options: a:No penalty — refusal is a constitutional right,b:A 1-year license revocation for first refusal,c:Only a fine with no license action,d:A warning only on the first offense
note: Delaware's implied consent law means driving on public roads constitutes consent to chemical testing. A first-offense refusal results in a 1-year license revocation separate from any DUI charge. Refusal can also be introduced as evidence against you in court.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum following distance recommended in Delaware for normal driving conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Delaware recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. In rain, fog, or heavy traffic — common near Delaware's urban corridors — increase to 4–6 seconds. More space equals more reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can you turn right on a red light in Delaware?
options: a:No, right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:Yes, after a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Yes, without stopping if no pedestrians are visible,d:Only on non-school days between 7 AM and 9 PM
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Delaware after a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic. Always check for 'No Turn on Red' signs before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver in Delaware is approaching a yield sign. What is required?
options: a:Stop completely regardless of traffic,b:Slow down and yield to traffic; stop only if necessary,c:Maintain speed and merge when safe,d:Flash headlights to signal your presence
note: A yield sign requires you to slow down and give the right of way to cross traffic or pedestrians. Stop if necessary to avoid a collision, but a full stop is not required when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are stopped at a Delaware intersection on a red light. The light turns green, but a large truck is still in the intersection. You should:
options: a:Honk to alert the truck and proceed — you have a green,b:Wait for the intersection to clear completely before entering,c:Flash your headlights and move forward,d:Change lanes to go around the truck
note: A green light gives you the right of way but does not guarantee the intersection is clear. Delaware's defensive driving principle requires you to ensure the path is fully clear — especially for large vehicles that take longer to clear — before entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action when you see a pedestrian with a visual impairment (white cane or guide dog) at a crosswalk in Delaware?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph and pass carefully,b:Stop completely and yield the roadway until the pedestrian has crossed safely,c:Honk to alert the pedestrian you are there,d:Yield only if the pedestrian is in your direct lane
note: Delaware law requires drivers to stop and yield completely to any pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog. These individuals are visually impaired and may not see your vehicle. Do not proceed until the pedestrian has completely and safely crossed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the shape and color of a warning sign in Delaware indicate?
options: a:Red octagon — stop required,b:Yellow diamond — potential hazard ahead,c:White rectangle — regulatory rule,d:Orange rectangle — construction zone
note: Yellow diamond-shaped signs are warning signs in Delaware and across the United States. They alert drivers to potential hazards ahead — curves, school zones, pedestrian crossings, merges, and more — and require extra alertness and often a reduction in speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Delaware, when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches from behind, you must:
options: a:Accelerate to the next intersection and pull off,b:Stop immediately in your current lane,c:Pull to the right side of the road and stop until it passes,d:Move to the left lane and reduce speed
note: Delaware law requires drivers to pull to the right side of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches from any direction. Remain stopped until the vehicle has fully passed before resuming travel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit on most Delaware rural roads and highways when no sign is posted?
options: a:45 mph,b:50 mph,c:55 mph,d:60 mph
note: Delaware's default speed limit on rural roads and highways without a posted limit is 55 mph. Always check for signs — many rural routes have posted limits that may differ from the 55 mph default.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in Delaware and see a flashing red traffic signal. What must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic, then proceed when safe — same as a stop sign,c:Treat it as a green light since no cross traffic is using the intersection,d:Stop only if another vehicle is approaching from the cross street
note: A flashing red signal must be treated as a stop sign in Delaware. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians in all directions, and proceed when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking on a street in Delaware, your wheels must be within how many inches of the curb?
options: a:6 inches,b:12 inches,c:18 inches,d:24 inches
note: Delaware law requires parallel-parked vehicles to be within 12 inches of the curb. Parking too far from the curb creates a hazard for passing vehicles and cyclists, and is a citable parking violation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Delaware, how many feet before a turn must you begin signaling?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet,d:300 feet
note: Delaware requires drivers to signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. Signaling early gives surrounding drivers and pedestrians adequate time to respond. Failing to signal is a moving violation in Delaware.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You see a person in a marked crosswalk in Delaware. What must you do?
options: a:Slow to 15 mph and proceed if the person is in a different lane,b:Stop and remain stopped until the person has completely crossed the road,c:Honk once and proceed if the way is clear,d:Yield only if they have already begun crossing
note: Delaware law requires drivers to stop and yield the entire roadway to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. You may not proceed until the pedestrian has completely crossed — even if they are in a different lane. Pedestrian right-of-way is absolute in a marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Delaware, what is the consequence of a first-offense DUI for an adult driver?
options: a:Warning letter and fine only,b:License revocation, fines, possible jail time, and mandatory alcohol treatment,c:Fine only — no license action on a first offense,d:Community service only
note: A first DUI conviction in Delaware results in license revocation, fines, possible jail time, and mandatory participation in an alcohol treatment program. Delaware's DUI penalties are designed to deter repeat offenses.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a Delaware multi-lane road, you see a sign that reads 'Keep Right Except to Pass.' This means:
options: a:You must always stay in the right lane regardless of speed,b:The left lane is reserved for passing only — use the right lane for normal travel,c:Right lane is for trucks only,d:The sign only applies to drivers below the speed limit
note: Delaware's 'Keep Right Except to Pass' rule requires drivers to use the right lane for normal travel on multi-lane roads and use the left lane only for passing. After passing, return to the right lane. This rule reduces tailgating and road rage on highways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching a railroad crossing in Delaware with flashing red lights and lowering gates. What must you do?
options: a:Stop before the gates fully lower and proceed before a train arrives,b:Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until the gates fully rise,c:Slow down to 10 mph and proceed quickly before the train arrives,d:Stop only if you can actually see a train approaching
note: When railroad crossing lights flash and gates begin lowering, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until the gates fully rise before proceeding. Never try to beat a train — trains cannot stop quickly and impacts are almost always fatal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal definition of reckless driving in Delaware?
options: a:Any speed exceeding the posted limit by 10 mph or more,b:Operating a vehicle with willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property,c:Any use of a cell phone while driving,d:Driving through a school zone above 25 mph
note: Reckless driving in Delaware is defined as operating a vehicle with willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property. It is a criminal offense — not just a traffic ticket — and can result in license suspension, fines, and possible imprisonment.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, when may motorists proceed?
options: a:As soon as all students are off the bus.,b:When the stop arm is retracted only.,c:Only after the lights are off
note: When a school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted. Do not move while the lights are still flashing, even if students appear to be clear of the road.

question: Why should you avoid sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.,b:Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks in their rearview mirrors.,c:Because large vehicles need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need a longer distance to stop. If you brake suddenly in front of them, they may not be able to stop in time, increasing the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving dangerous?
options: a:It causes the driver to worry about call costs.,b:It draws other drivers' attention away from the road.,c:It occupies the driver's eyes
note: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it distracts you visually, manually, and mentally. Looking at the phone takes your eyes off the road, handling it takes your hands off the wheel, and focusing on the conversation takes your mind off driving, all of which greatly increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, you should begin your turn from:
options: a:The lane closest to the centerline.,b:The right-hand side of the road.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: For a left turn from a two-way street, you should start from the lane closest to the centerline. This position shortens the turn, keeps you predictable to other drivers, and helps you enter the correct lane on the new road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked cars to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,c:Steer closer to the parked cars than the oncoming vehicles.
note: When there are oncoming vehicles on your left and parked cars on your right, steer a middle course between them. This gives you the greatest possible space on both sides and reduces the chance of sideswiping a parked car or drifting into oncoming traffic.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you use to help others see you?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: As daylight fades or in low‑light conditions, you should turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road. Parking lights and emergency flashers are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

question: Which statement about braking and accelerating is correct?
options: a:Always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.,b:Use your left foot to brake.,c:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake so you don’t accidentally press both pedals at once. Apply the brakes smoothly and gradually to maintain control and give drivers behind you time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in a construction zone, what's the best approach?
options: a:Slightly increase your speed.,b:Expect the unexpected and proceed with extra caution.,c:Expect workers to yield to motorists.
note: In construction zones, slow down, be prepared for sudden stops, lane shifts, and workers or equipment entering the roadway. Expect the unexpected and proceed with extra caution to protect both workers and drivers.

question: What important action should you take when making a turn?
options: a:Always move to the left lane.,b:Check traffic in all directions.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Before making any turn, you must check traffic in all directions: ahead, behind, and to both sides. This helps you judge gaps, see pedestrians, cyclists, and other vehicles, and adjust your speed and lane position so you can turn safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you enter a designated left-turn lane with oncoming traffic, what should you do before turning?
options: a:Turn your front wheels left to be ready to turn.,b:Move to the left of the center lane to prepare.,c:Signal about 100 feet before and keep wheels straight until you actually turn.
note: When waiting to turn left, signal in advance (about 100 feet before the turn where practical) and keep your front wheels pointed straight. If another vehicle hits you from behind, straight wheels help prevent your car from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When following a large truck on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Follow more closely than you would a passenger vehicle.,b:Always remain to the right of the truck and wait to pass.,c:Follow farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop and have big blind spots directly in front, behind, and along the sides. To stay safe, leave extra following distance behind a truck so you have more time to react and can see the road ahead.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction because of standing water, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed to improve traction.,b:Apply the brakes firmly to regain control.,c:Slow down gradually and avoid using the brakes.
note: When your tires ride on top of water (hydroplaning), sudden braking or steering can cause a skid. Ease off the accelerator, keep the wheels straight, and slow down gradually without braking until you regain traction.

question: What happens as your BAC increases?
options: a:You become more sober.,b:You become more intoxicated.,c:You become more coordinated.
note: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) goes up, judgment, reaction time, coordination, and vision all get worse. Even small increases in BAC mean more impairment and a higher risk of a crash.

question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed if it is clear.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:Increase your speed.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is safe and the way is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection; it does not give you permission to speed up.

question: What is a common effect of excessive speed?
options: a:It often leads to high-risk decision-making.,b:It increases your ability to react to hazards.,c:It does not increase crash risk.
note: Driving too fast reduces the time you have to see and react to hazards and often leads to risky maneuvers like hard braking or sudden lane changes. Excessive speed greatly increases both the chance and severity of crashes.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the lane adjacent to the solid line.,b:Permitted from the lane adjacent to the broken line.,c:Prohibited from both directions.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line, and drivers on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:
options: a:Both lanes of traffic go in the same direction.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing is permitted when it is safe.
note: A broken yellow line between two lanes means the lanes carry traffic in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it is safe and clear. You must still check for oncoming traffic and only pass when you have enough space.

question: To help prevent hydroplaning on wet roads you should:
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,c:Slow down.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds. To help prevent hydroplaning, slow down when roads are wet and avoid sudden acceleration, braking, or sharp steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Exiting a freeway on a ramp that curves downhill, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until you are in the curve to begin braking.,b:Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.,c:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.
note: When exiting a freeway on a downhill curve, you should reduce speed to a safe level before entering the curve. Braking hard while in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially on a downgrade.

question: To avoid hydroplaning in wet conditions, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at speeds suitable for ideal conditions.,b:Apply brakes as soon as the car starts to skid.,c:Slow down.
note: To avoid hydroplaning, drive more slowly in wet conditions so your tires can maintain contact with the road surface. Adjust your speed below what you would use in ideal conditions and avoid sudden maneuvers.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They are less predictable and may not judge traffic situations well.,b:Both of the above.,c:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.
note: Drivers should give extra space to children on bicycles because they are smaller and harder to see, and they are often less predictable in how they ride. Children may suddenly swerve, stop, or enter the roadway without checking for traffic, so giving them more room and slowing down helps prevent collisions.

question: When should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.,c:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
note: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway, your wheels should not be pointed straight ahead. Turn the wheels so that if the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic and toward the curb or edge of the road. On level roads without a curb, you may leave the wheels straight, but on hills you must turn them for safety.

question: What are "no zones" around large trucks?
options: a:They have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.,b:They are areas where cars have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close they restrict the truck driver's ability to maneuver safely.
note: “No zones” are the large blind spots and danger areas around trucks and other large vehicles. If you drive in these areas, the truck driver may not see you, or you may be so close that the truck cannot stop or turn safely. Stay out of these zones by not lingering alongside trucks and by leaving extra following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in residential areas?
options: a:30 mph,b:25 mph,c:20 mph
note: In many U.S. states, the general speed limit in residential areas is 25 mph unless signs show a different limit. Residential areas often have children, pedestrians, and cars entering or leaving driveways, so driving at or below 25 mph and staying alert helps you stop in time for unexpected hazards.

question: When reversing, what is the correct technique?
options: a:Press hard on the gas pedal to maneuver quickly.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Look through the rear window while backing up.
note: When reversing, you should turn your head and look directly through the rear window while backing up slowly. Mirrors alone do not show everything behind your vehicle, and using too much gas can make it hard to control your speed and stop quickly. Move at a walking pace so you can react to people, vehicles, or objects behind you.

question: Only which factor can lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat.,b:Drinking caffeine.,c:Time.
note: Only time lowers your BAC. Your body must metabolize the alcohol, and this happens at a fairly steady rate. Eating food, drinking coffee, taking a cold shower, or exercising may make you feel more awake, but they do not speed up how fast alcohol leaves your bloodstream.

question: When conditions require you to drive with headlights on, which lights should you use?
options: a:Use your high beams.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your low beams.
note: When conditions require headlights (such as rain, fog, snow, or darkness), you should normally use low beam headlights. Low beams give you good visibility without creating excessive glare or reflection. High beams can reflect off rain, fog, or snow and make it harder to see, and parking lights alone are not legal or safe for driving because they do not provide enough light or make you visible enough to others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a Yield sign you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to crossing traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: At a Yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let crossing or merging traffic go first if it is close enough to be a hazard. If there is no traffic or pedestrians that would conflict with your movement, you may proceed without stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you end up?
options: a:Turn into the first lane of the one-way street.,b:Turn into any lane.,c:Turn into the second lane.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, start from the left lane of the two-way street and turn into the first legal lane on the one-way street, usually the lane closest to the left curb. Turning into the nearest lane helps keep traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles in other lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means you must:
options: a:You are traveling in the wrong direction.,b:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign (come to a complete stop).,c:Not proceed until it changes to green.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. After stopping, yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in or approaching the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: A steady red arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:Drivers may not proceed in the indicated direction until the signal changes.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.,c:Drivers may proceed without stopping.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to go in the direction of the arrow until it turns green or a green arrow appears. You must wait; no turns or movements are allowed in that direction on a steady red arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic, what is the most likely result?
options: a:You may interfere with traffic and could receive a citation.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You will demonstrate defensive driving skills.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because other drivers may need to brake or change lanes suddenly. If you unnecessarily block or interfere with traffic, you can be cited. When safe and legal, match the speed of traffic up to the posted limit.

question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.,b:It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,c:So other road users know your intentions.
note: You should keep your turn signal on throughout the entire turn or lane change so that other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians clearly understand what you plan to do. Signaling continuously gives others time to react and helps prevent collisions.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed.,b:Speed up to pass hazards quickly.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: On wet or icy roads, your tires have less grip, so it is easier to skid or lose control. Reducing your speed gives you more time to react and helps you stop more safely. Always adjust your speed to road and weather conditions, even if it is below the posted limit.

question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,b:Slow down but never stop.,c:Yield the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection or roadway you are entering. Proceed only when it is safe and will not force others to slow or stop suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green traffic light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Follow the vehicle ahead and enter the intersection.,b:Turn left and find another route.,c:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it, even with a green light. If traffic ahead is stopped and you would be left blocking the cross street, stay behind the stop line until there is enough space to drive all the way through.

question: When must you use low beam headlights?
options: a:On a lighted street.,b:In fog.,c:On a freeway.
note: In fog you must use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off the water droplets in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams give better visibility in fog, rain, snow, or mist and make your vehicle more visible to others.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,b:Other drivers when they want to slow down.,c:So the truck driver has room to stop and because trucks need longer stopping distances.
note: Large trucks are heavy and need a much longer distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver room to slow or stop safely and reduces the risk of a rear-end collision if traffic suddenly changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the interstate, how can you avoid merging traffic entering from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Slow down and stay in the right lane.,b:Change lanes to the left when traffic permits.,c:Maintain your speed and lane position always.
note: On interstates, traffic often enters from the right. When it is safe, moving one lane to the left creates space for merging vehicles and reduces conflicts. If you cannot move left, be prepared to adjust your speed slightly to help them merge smoothly.

question: How can you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Merge into a different lane when possible to create a gap.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: When vehicles are entering a freeway, help them merge safely by creating space. If possible, change to a lane farther from the on-ramp to open a gap. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed slightly so there is a safe space for the entering vehicle to merge.

question: What is true about large trucks compared to passenger vehicles?
options: a:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,b:They all have air brakes that allow very quick stops.,c:They take longer to stop than passenger cars.
note: Large trucks are heavier and need more distance to stop than passenger cars, especially at higher speeds. Even with good brakes, their weight means they cannot stop as quickly as smaller vehicles, so you should avoid cutting in front of them or braking suddenly.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you should:
options: a:Expect a traffic light ahead.,b:Not pass.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is prohibited from your lane. You may cross it only to turn left safely into or out of a driveway or side road, but not to pass another vehicle.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, drivers approaching from either direction must:
options: a:Stop only if they are traveling in the same direction as the bus.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop only if there are children in the street.,c:Stop when the bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical median or barrier.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, drivers from both directions must stop on undivided roads. On a divided highway with a physical median or barrier, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop; oncoming traffic on the other side of the median may proceed with caution.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Blind spots can be checked using only your rearview mirror.,b:Blind spots are eliminated with one outside mirror.,c:Large trucks have larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much bigger blind spots on all sides than passenger cars, especially on the right side and directly behind the truck. Avoid lingering in these areas where the truck driver may not see you.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what is true?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the right.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the left.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You must stay in your lane and may only cross these lines when turning left safely into or out of a driveway or side road where it is permitted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on city streets?
options: a:So you can keep up with traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter mile to stop.,c:To see potential hazards earlier.
note: On freeways you travel at higher speeds, so hazards, slowdowns, and merging traffic develop more quickly. Looking farther ahead gives you more time to see problems early and adjust smoothly, instead of braking or swerving at the last second.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, you should turn your front wheels:
options: a:Toward the center of the road (left).,b:Toward the side of the road (right).,c:Straight ahead.
note: When parking downhill with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the side of the road (right). If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you not start across an intersection because you might block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Unless you entered on a green light.,b:Under any circumstances you should avoid entering if you cannot clear it before the light turns red.,c:Unless you entered on a yellow light.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to clear it completely, even if the light is green. Entering when you cannot get all the way through can leave you blocking cross traffic when the light changes, which is unsafe and often illegal.

question: When is a wet highway surface most likely to be especially slippery?
options: a:If it has been raining for one to two hours.,b:If it has been raining several hours.,c:If it has just begun to rain.
note: When rain first begins, oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the water and create a very slick film. Until continued rain washes this away, traction is reduced and it is easier to skid, so you should slow down and drive smoothly.

question: Even a small amount of alcohol in the blood can affect a driver's what?
options: a:Knowledge.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Judgment and physical coordination.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can slow your reactions and affect your judgment and coordination. This makes it harder to steer, brake, and make safe decisions, increasing the risk of a crash.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Ease up on the gas pedal.,c:Brake as hard as possible.
note: When a vehicle begins to skid, smoothly ease off the accelerator (and off the brake if you were braking) so the tires can regain traction, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. Do not slam on the brakes or turn off the ignition, as that can cause a complete loss of control.

question: On the highway, consistently scanning far ahead of your vehicle primarily helps to:
options: a:Help you keep up with traffic.,b:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,c:Allow you to spot upcoming police officers.
note: On highways you should look well ahead so you can see slow traffic, lane closures, or hazards early. This gives you time to adjust speed or change lanes smoothly, which reduces sudden braking or swerving and lowers the risk of collisions.

question: Roads are especially slippery just after it starts to rain. When the road is slippery, you should:
options: a:Test your tires' traction by accelerating while going uphill.,b:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.,c:Avoid fast turns or sudden stops and drive more slowly.
note: Right after it starts to rain, oil and dirt mix with water and make the road very slippery. You should slow down, avoid fast turns, and avoid sudden braking or acceleration so your tires can maintain traction and you are less likely to skid.

question: To stay aware of traffic behind you you should:
options: a:Turn and look out your back window each time.,b:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.
note: To stay aware of traffic behind you, check your mirrors frequently—about every few seconds and before changing lanes, slowing, or turning. This helps you know where other vehicles are and react safely if someone is following too closely or approaching quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but do not see a gap in traffic, you should:
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,b:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.,c:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match freeway traffic and merge into a safe gap. If you do not see a gap, slow down on the ramp and wait for one; avoid stopping at the end of the ramp because it makes it hard to accelerate and merge safely.

question: If you're about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Brace yourself by pressing into the seat back.,b:Press your head against the head restraint.,c:Release your seat belt.
note: In a rear-end collision, you should keep your seat belt fastened and press your body and head firmly against the seat and head restraint. This helps your body move with the seat and reduces the whipping motion of your neck and spine. Never release your seat belt; it is your primary protection in any crash.

question: Children under age 16 in a moving vehicle must:
options: a:Be restrained at all times.,b:Be restrained only on freeways.,c:Be restrained at the parent's discretion.
note: Children must always be properly restrained in a moving vehicle, using the correct child safety seat, booster, or seat belt for their age, size, and weight. This applies on all roads, not just freeways, and is not left to a parent’s discretion because proper restraints greatly reduce the risk of injury or death in a crash.

question: After a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage, what should you do if it is safe?
options: a:Not move your vehicle for any reason.,b:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,c:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.
note: After a minor crash with no injuries, if the vehicles are drivable and it is safe, you should move them out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a safe area. This helps prevent additional collisions and keeps traffic flowing. Leave vehicles in the lane only if they cannot be moved or it is unsafe to do so.

question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:The railroad crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.,b:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely clear the tracks.,c:You are transporting two or more young children.
note: You must not enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough space on the far side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks. Stopping on the tracks is extremely dangerous because a train cannot stop quickly. Always wait until you can fully clear the crossing before proceeding.

question: To help avoid skids on slippery surfaces, what should you do?
options: a:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,b:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: To avoid skids on slippery roads, slow down before you reach curves and intersections so you can steer smoothly without hard braking. Braking or accelerating suddenly while turning increases the chance of losing traction and skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is true about roadwork (work) zones?
options: a:Slow only if you think workers are present.,b:Fines are always the same as normal conditions.,c:You must slow down for the Cone Zone.
note: In work zones, you must slow down and drive with extra caution whenever you see cones, signs, or workers, even if you are not sure workers are immediately next to the lane. Many states increase fines in work zones to encourage drivers to reduce speed and pay close attention.

question: As you near the crest of a hill, you should:
options: a:Speed up slightly.,b:Keep a steady speed.,c:Be prepared to stop if necessary.
note: As you approach the top of a hill, your view of oncoming traffic, stopped vehicles, or obstacles is limited. You should reduce speed and be ready to stop if needed so you can react safely to anything that appears as you reach the crest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Rely only on the left side mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check the blind spot.,c:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This shoulder check lets you see into your blind spot, where vehicles may not appear in your mirrors.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:An antihistamine.,b:A depressant.,c:A stimulant.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain function, reduces judgment, and delays reaction time, which makes driving unsafe even at relatively low blood alcohol levels.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line on your side is broken, you may cross it to pass another vehicle on the left, but only when the lane is clear and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Only begin to prepare to slow down.
note: If a child looks like they may run into the street, you must be ready to stop immediately and warn them. A sharp blast of the horn alerts the child and others to danger. At the same time, you should cover the brake and be prepared to slow or stop quickly to avoid a collision.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, what is still required for safety?
options: a:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,b:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,c:Seat belts should still be worn.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. Seat belts keep you properly positioned so the airbag can protect you and reduce the risk of being thrown from the vehicle. You must always wear your seat belt, even in vehicles equipped with airbags.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to reduce collision risk?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at oncoming headlights.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night, visibility is reduced and it is harder to see hazards in time. Increasing your following distance gives you more time to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Use low or high beams appropriately, but do not look directly at oncoming headlights, as this can temporarily blind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see a lane sign showing an arrow with the word "ONLY" beneath it, you should:
options: a:Look for a destination sign to follow instead of the arrow.,b:Always change lanes when you see it.,c:Travel only in the direction indicated by the arrow.
note: A lane control sign with an arrow and the word “ONLY” means that traffic in that lane must go only in the direction of the arrow. You may not go straight or turn in any other direction from that lane. If you need a different direction, change lanes safely before reaching the intersection.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean for a left turn?
options: a:You should speed up to make the turn before it changes.,b:You don't need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.,c:Prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic — the protected turn is ending.
note: A solid yellow left-turn arrow warns that the protected green arrow phase is ending. You should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. After the yellow arrow, you may lose the protected turn and may have to turn only when there is a safe gap.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is sliding left in a skid, what should you do?
options: a:Not turn the wheel.,b:Turn the steering wheel left (in direction of skid).,c:Turn the wheel right (away from skid).
note: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid, you should steer in the same direction the rear is sliding. If the rear slides left, gently turn the steering wheel to the left while easing off the accelerator. This helps the vehicle straighten out. Avoid hard braking unless your vehicle has ABS and you are braking firmly in an emergency.

question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:Only if you are stopped and cited.,c:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
note: Drivers must carry proof of financial responsibility, usually an insurance card, whenever they drive. You are required to show this proof to a law enforcement officer if you are stopped for a traffic violation or involved in a collision. Failing to provide proof can result in citations or other penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, do not move back into the right lane until you are safely ahead of the vehicle you passed. A good rule is to wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle clearly in your inside rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off.

question: Broken yellow lines on the roadway are used to:
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,b:Indicate no passing zones.,c:Separate traffic moving in opposite directions
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. When the yellow line is broken, it means passing is allowed when it can be done safely and legally. Solid yellow lines, or combinations of solid and broken, are used to mark no-passing zones or restrict passing from one direction.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what is the safest course of action before driving?
options: a:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Loudly play the radio while driving so you won’t think about your argument.
note: Strong emotions like anger, sadness, or excitement can distract you, slow your reactions, and lead to risky decisions. If you are upset after an argument, the safest choice is to wait and give yourself time to calm down before driving. You should only drive when you can focus fully on the road and other users.

question: While in a motor vehicle on a highway, it is:
options: a:Legal to drink alcohol while driving if you are not intoxicated.,b:Legal to drink alcohol if you are not the driver.,c:Illegal to drink or possess open containers of alcohol.
note: Open container laws generally make it illegal for anyone in a moving vehicle on a public road to drink alcohol or possess an open container of alcohol, regardless of whether they are the driver or a passenger. Even if a driver is not yet legally intoxicated, drinking while driving is unsafe and typically prohibited. Operating a vehicle while impaired by alcohol or drugs is always illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
options: a:Only during the day.,b:Only under ideal driving conditions.,c:Only during the night.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions, not a required speed. You must always adjust your speed for traffic, weather, visibility, and road conditions, and drive slower when conditions are not ideal, even if that is below the posted limit.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only if the pedestrians wave to the driver.,c:Only if the pedestrians are not using a phone.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks. You must stop or slow as needed for any pedestrian who is in the crosswalk or approaching your lane, regardless of whether they signal to you or are using a phone. Pedestrian safety takes priority whenever they are lawfully crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing, what should you do?
options: a:Only signal and assume it's safe.,b:Change lanes quickly without checking mirrors.,c:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you must signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors, so a quick head check is essential to be sure there is no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle beside you before you move into another lane.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,b:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,c:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
note: Orange signs and cones indicate a work zone. You must be prepared for workers on or near the roadway, construction vehicles entering or leaving, lane shifts, and reduced speeds. Slow down, follow posted work-zone speed limits, and be ready to stop or change lanes as directed by signs or flaggers.

question: When may you cross double yellow centerlines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:The yellow line next to the opposite side is broken.,b:The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,c:The vehicle in front of you moves right to let you pass.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe and legal to do so. If the yellow line on your side is solid, you must not cross it to pass, even if the line on the opposite side is broken.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.,b:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.,c:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the road even if there is no marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a full stop and remain stopped until the light stops flashing.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe. You do not stay stopped indefinitely; you go after yielding the right-of-way.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Allow a larger following distance.,b:Drive more slowly.,c:Be ready to use your horn.
note: Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly and are less visible than cars, so you should allow a larger following distance—at least three to four seconds. This extra space gives you more time to react if the motorcycle slows or stops suddenly.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part (lap and shoulder) seat belt system, how should you use it?
options: a:Use only the lap belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: If your vehicle has both a lap belt and a shoulder belt, you should always wear both. The lap belt keeps your lower body in place, and the shoulder belt helps protect your head and chest in a crash.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if traffic signals favor the pedestrian.,b:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,c:At all times to avoid striking them
note: Drivers must always do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally or against a signal. Yielding to pedestrians whenever there is a risk of conflict helps prevent serious injury or death.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat an intersection where the traffic signal is not operating?
options: a:Drive quickly through to get out of the way of other vehicles.,b:If the intersection is clear, proceed through without stopping.,c:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
note: When a traffic signal is completely dark or not operating, you must treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed only when it is your turn and it is safe, yielding the right-of-way to any vehicles or pedestrians already in or clearly approaching the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may safely return to your lane after passing another vehicle when:
options: a:You have cleared the other vehicle's front bumper.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are about three seconds ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the passed vehicle (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off.

question: If there is a deep puddle ahead, you should:
options: a:Shift into neutral while driving through it.,b:Avoid it if possible.,c:Maintain the posted speed to make it through.
note: Deep water can cause hydroplaning, loss of steering control, or engine and brake damage. If you can safely avoid a deep puddle, you should go around it or choose another route rather than driving through it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do before moving over?
options: a:Slow down abruptly.,b:Only check the inside rearview mirror.,c:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and then look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check lets you see into your blind spot and helps ensure the lane is clear before you move over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the posted speed limit in Delaware school zones?
options: a:20 mph.,b:15 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: In Delaware, the standard posted speed limit in school zones is 20 mph when children are present or when the school zone is active. You must slow to this lower speed and drive with extra caution near schools and playgrounds because children may enter the roadway unexpectedly.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:All pedestrians and drivers to respect your right-of-way.,b:Driving closely to parked cars to allow more room for moving traffic.,c:A person or vehicle unexpectedly entering your lane.
note: When passing a row of parked vehicles, you should be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane from between or around the parked cars. Slow down, leave extra space, and scan carefully so you can stop or steer safely if someone steps or pulls out unexpectedly.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the arm is retracted and the bus moves.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing, the stop arm is retracted, and the bus starts moving again. This rule protects children who may be crossing the road in front of or behind the bus.

question: What is an effect of tailgating other drivers?
options: a:It reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.,b:It can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,c:It cannot result in a traffic citation.
note: Tailgating, or following too closely, can anger and frustrate other drivers and may trigger aggressive driving or road rage. It also greatly reduces your time to react and stop, increasing the risk of a rear-end collision and possible traffic citations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian starts crossing during a 'Don't Walk' flash and is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before proceeding.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.
note: Even with a green light, yield to pedestrians already in the intersection until they finish crossing.

question: What is the best action if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Open a window.
note: If you grow tired while driving, stop in a safe place to rest or change drivers; temporary measures are not substitutes for sleep.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, at what minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) does driving become illegal?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older in most U.S. states, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Impairment can begin at lower levels, but 0.08 is the standard legal limit for DUI for adults.

question: If the rear of your vehicle skids left, which way should you steer?
options: a:Steer to the left to correct the skid.,b:Steer to the right.,c:Tap brakes lightly and shift into neutral.
note: If the rear of your vehicle skids, you should steer in the same direction the rear is sliding. If the rear skids left, steer left. This helps realign the vehicle with your direction of travel and regain control.

question: Which substances can impair driving ability?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many substances can impair driving, including tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, and some cough or cold medicines with codeine or antihistamines. Always read labels and follow medical advice before driving after taking any drug.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic after parking at a curb, how do you merge safely?
options: a:Wait for a gap large enough to get up to the speed of traffic.,b:Should drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass then drive into the lane.
note: When pulling out from a curb, wait for a gap that allows you to signal, pull out smoothly, and accelerate to match the speed of traffic without forcing others to brake or swerve.

question: When following another vehicle at night, you should:
options: a:Always use high beams.,b:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,c:Use your high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: When you are following another vehicle at night, you must use low beam headlights so your lights do not shine directly into the mirrors of the driver ahead. High beams can cause glare and temporarily blind the other driver, increasing the risk of a crash.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights, you must yield right-of-way by:
options: a:Moving into the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.,b:Driving as close as possible to the right edge of the road and stopping.,c:Stopping immediately even if you are in an intersection.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using its siren and flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge or curb and stopping. Do not stop in an intersection; instead, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: At a school crossing sign (pentagon-shaped), what should drivers do?
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop even without a stop sign.
note: A pentagon-shaped sign warns of a school zone or school crossing. When you see this sign, slow down, watch carefully for children who may enter the road unexpectedly, and be ready to stop if necessary, especially during school hours or when children are present.

question: A red octagon-shaped sign always means:
options: a:Stop.,b:Do not enter.,c:One-way.
note: An octagon-shaped sign is used only for STOP signs. When you see a red octagon, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any pedestrians or other vehicles with the right-of-way.

question: Defensive drivers:
options: a:Assume other drivers will always do the right thing.,b:Expect no breaks and give none.,c:Consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.
note: Defensive drivers constantly scan the road and think ahead about what other drivers, pedestrians, or cyclists might do. They do not assume others will always follow the rules; instead, they stay prepared to slow, stop, or change lanes to avoid hazards and reduce the chance of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you not do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and return to your desired exit.,b:Continue on the freeway and find another route.,c:Back up on the road or shoulder.
note: Do not back up on a freeway or shoulder; continue to the next exit and safely return to your destination.

question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Use the inside rearview mirror.,b:Use only your side mirror.,c:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
note: Mirrors alone cannot show everything around your vehicle; there are areas to the sides that mirrors do not cover, called blind spots. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
note: You should not change lanes while you are driving through an intersection because traffic and pedestrians may be crossing from several directions, increasing the risk of a collision. Instead, travel straight through the intersection in your lane, then change lanes once you are clear. Whenever you change lanes, always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, it is safe to return to the right lane when:
options: a:You can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:About three seconds after completing the pass.,c:You can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: After passing another vehicle on the left, do not move back into the right lane until you can see the front of the passed vehicle (or its headlights at night) in your inside rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and reduces the chance of cutting it off.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout, how should you use the brakes?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Use the brakes lightly.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.
note: If a tire suddenly blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Do not slam on the brakes, as this can cause a skid or loss of control. Instead, ease your foot off the accelerator and use the brakes lightly, if needed, to slow down gradually while you steer to a safe place off the road.

question: A driver should keep watch:
options: a:Directly in front of the car at all times.,b:Only at the middle of the road.,c:All around your vehicle — ahead, to the sides, and behind.
note: Safe drivers scan the entire traffic scene — far ahead, to both sides, and behind — instead of staring in just one place. You should look well ahead down the road while also checking your mirrors and side areas so you can spot hazards early and have time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle moving in the same direction, it is safe to move back into the right lane when:
options: a:You can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:You can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:About three seconds after passing.
note: After you pass another vehicle, do not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space and are not cutting the other driver off. Always check your mirrors and blind spot before returning to the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle?
options: a:Speed up to clear the lane.,b:Pull as far to the right as possible and stop.,c:Move into the right lane and continue slowly until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as you safely can and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs you otherwise.

question: What effect does drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:Make you feel better.,b:Help you to be a better driver.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Drowsiness makes driving dangerous because it slows your reaction time, reduces your awareness of what is happening around you, and impairs your judgment. A drowsy driver may drift out of their lane, miss traffic signals, or react too slowly to hazards, increasing the risk of a crash.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, what lights should you turn on?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Headlights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: In dust, smoke, or similar low-visibility conditions, you should turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you more easily. Use low beams so the light does not reflect back and further reduce your visibility. Headlights make your vehicle more visible from the front and rear.

question: Regulatory road signs typically have what background color?
options: a:Green.,b:White.,c:Yellow.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do (such as speed limits, no parking, or one-way). In the U.S., these are typically white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green letters or symbols, so white is the correct background color.

question: During rainy weather, when are turns or stops most hazardous?
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:One half hour after the rain stops.,c:After it has been raining all day.
note: When rain first begins, oil and residue on the road mix with the water and rise to the surface, making the pavement especially slick. This is why the first 20–30 minutes of rain are usually the most hazardous for turning and stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a steady yellow light at an intersection, if you have not entered, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce speed and continue through the intersection regardless.,c:Stop safely if you can.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should stop if you can do so safely, rather than trying to speed up and risk entering on a red light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.,c:At the posted speed regardless of traffic flow.
note: When using a freeway on-ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic already on the freeway. Entering at or near the speed of traffic allows you to merge smoothly and reduces the need for other drivers to brake or swerve.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you do?
options: a:Keep front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb but not use the parking brake.,b:Use the parking brake and leave the vehicle in Park; position wheels so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if brakes fail.,c:Have a rear wheel touch the curb.
note: On any hill, always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in Park (or in gear with a manual transmission). Turn the front wheels so that if the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll toward the curb or shoulder and away from moving traffic.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads, what is the best action?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Slow down.
note: On wet roads, slowing down is the best way to reduce the risk of hydroplaning. Lower speed allows your tires to maintain better contact with the road and gives you more time to react. Avoid sudden steering, braking, or acceleration, which can cause you to lose traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no passing zone, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Slow down to let the other driver safely return to the driving lane.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: If another driver is passing you in a no‑passing zone, you should not speed up or block them. Instead, maintain a steady path and, if needed, gently slow down so they can complete the pass and return to the lane as safely and quickly as possible. This reduces the time both vehicles are exposed to oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate where there is no acceleration lane, you should:
options: a:Use the shoulder to gain speed before merging.,b:Only enter the interstate after identifying a gap in traffic and then speed to match flow.,c:Immediately enter the far-right lane and speed up regardless of gaps.
note: When there is no acceleration lane, you must wait for a safe gap in traffic before entering the interstate. Once a gap appears, enter and accelerate promptly to match the speed of traffic. Never use the shoulder to gain speed and never force your way in without a safe opening.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your driving lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:When the driver you passed signals for you to return.,c:When you have signaled for three seconds.
note: After passing, it is safe to return to your lane only when you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed, including its headlights, in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space ahead of that vehicle to move back without cutting them off.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting choice is best?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare, helping you see better. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see.

question: Why should you keep the inside of your windows clean if someone has been smoking?
options: a:Dust tends to settle on the insides of car windows.,b:Smoking causes a film to build up on the glass inside the vehicle.,c:The stale smell can be distracting.
note: Smoking leaves a residue on the inside of windows that creates a hazy film. This film scatters light and reduces visibility, especially at night or in bright sun. Keeping the inside glass clean helps you see clearly and drive more safely.

question: If your tires feel like they're losing contact with the road surface, what should you do first?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.,c:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.
