note: If your tires are losing contact with the road (such as during hydroplaning), gently ease your foot off the accelerator and avoid braking or turning suddenly. This helps the tires regain traction smoothly and reduces the chance of skidding or losing control.

question: What is the effect of slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events?
options: a:Prevents rear-end collisions.,b:Causes traffic congestion.,c:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.
note: Slowing down just to look at a collision or something unusual on the road is called rubbernecking. It distracts you from driving, often causes sudden slowdowns, and leads to traffic congestion and sometimes additional crashes behind you. Keep your attention on the road ahead and maintain a steady, safe speed.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Missing an exit.,b:Being late for appointments.,c:Falling asleep and crashing.
note: Driving while tired slows your reactions, affects your judgment, and can cause you to drift out of your lane or even fall asleep at the wheel. This greatly increases the risk of a serious crash. If you feel drowsy, stop in a safe place and rest rather than continuing to drive.

question: You are driving defensively when you:
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.,c:Look only at the car directly in front of you.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, checking mirrors, and watching around your vehicle so you can spot hazards early and react in time. Keeping your eyes moving helps you avoid surprises and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road.,b:Look toward the center of the roadway.,c:Look straight ahead at the lights.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, do not stare into the lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This reduces glare, helps you avoid being temporarily blinded, and still keeps you correctly positioned in your lane.

question: A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross before you make a right turn. What should you do?
options: a:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,b:Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.,c:Wait until the person crosses the street.
note: A pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane is blind or visually impaired and always has the right‑of‑way. Stop and wait until the person has completely crossed before you turn. Do not tell them when to cross; they rely on their own training, signals, and the dog’s guidance.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line next to your lane is broken, you may cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if the lane is clear and it is safe. Passing on the right is only allowed in specific situations and is not what a broken yellow centerline indicates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an alley or driveway across a sidewalk to enter traffic, you should:
options: a:Expect pedestrians to yield to you.,b:Only stop if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,c:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.
note: When you are leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot and must cross a sidewalk, you must stop before driving onto the sidewalk area. Yield to all pedestrians on the sidewalk, then proceed slowly and carefully into the roadway when it is safe.

question: When should you allow extra following distance for the vehicle ahead?
options: a:When following a passenger vehicle.,b:When following a station wagon.,c:When following a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are smaller, harder to see, and can stop or swerve more quickly than larger vehicles. Leave extra following distance behind a motorcycle so you have more time to react if the rider slows or stops suddenly.

question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?
options: a:Driving in both directions may pass.,b:Next to the broken line may pass.,c:Next to the solid line may pass.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and not allowed for traffic on the side with the solid line. You may cross the broken yellow line to pass when it is safe and legal, but you must not cross the solid yellow line to pass.

question: Which factor affects how quickly alcohol is absorbed into a person's system?
options: a:Intelligence,b:Height,c:Weight
note: A person’s weight is one of the main factors that affects how quickly alcohol is absorbed and how strongly it affects them. In general, a smaller person will reach a higher blood alcohol concentration than a larger person after drinking the same amount. Other important factors include sex, how much food is in the stomach, and how many drinks were consumed. Only time can reduce the amount of alcohol in the body.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Construction zone signs are normally what shape and color?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black symbols.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Construction and work zone signs are usually diamond-shaped or rectangular with an orange background and black letters or symbols. They warn you of road work, lane closures, workers, or changes in normal traffic patterns so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: On a green traffic arrow, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Only yield to pedestrians in the intersection.,b:Yield to any vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Wait four seconds before starting the turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in the intersection or still clearing it. Look carefully, make sure the path is clear, and then complete your turn when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always travel at what speed?
options: a:At the posted speed limit no matter what.,b:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you even if above limit.,c:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
note: You must always drive at a speed that is safe for current road, traffic, and weather conditions, and never faster than the posted speed limit. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility, this often means driving below the speed limit so you have enough time to react and stop safely.

question: When stopped at a railroad with double tracks, when may you proceed?
options: a:As soon as one train has passed.,b:Only when the train is out of sight.,c:Only when you are sure no trains are approaching on either track and the passing train is well clear.
note: At crossings with more than one track, a second train can come from either direction, sometimes hidden by the first train. You must wait until the first train has completely passed and you have a clear view of all tracks in both directions, and are sure no other trains are approaching, before proceeding.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing outside a crosswalk, what must you do?
options: a:Must stop for them.,b:Should honk your horn at them.,c:Do not have to stop for them.
note: Drivers must exercise due care to avoid hitting pedestrians, even when pedestrians are crossing illegally or outside a crosswalk. If a pedestrian is in your path, you must slow or stop as needed to avoid a collision and allow them to cross safely.

question: When the center of the roadway has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line, and the broken line is next to your lane, it means:
options: a:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,b:You may only make right turns here.,c:You are in a passing zone and may pass on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
note: A solid yellow line means no passing from that side; a broken yellow line means passing is allowed when safe. If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass vehicles ahead of you on the left when there is enough clear distance and no oncoming traffic.

question: Why should you not use high beams in fog or mist?
options: a:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,b:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,c:The light will reflect back into your eyes.
note: In fog or mist, high beams shine into the tiny water droplets and reflect back toward you, creating glare and making it harder to see the road. Use low beams in fog so the light aims down at the road surface and improves your visibility.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see, you should:
options: a:Slow down whenever you see one in the distance.,b:Share a lane with a motorcycle to give it space.,c:Make constant visual checks for them.
note: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are smaller and can be easily hidden in blind spots or blended into traffic. You should frequently check mirrors, blind spots, and the road ahead specifically for them, and give them a full lane and extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is required when turning left at an intersection?
options: a:You should yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians.
note: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until there is a safe gap and the crosswalk is clear before completing your turn.

question: Which action helps you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Tailgate the driver ahead.,b:Relax and focus on driving.,c:Drive above the posted speed limit.
note: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, stay relaxed, allow extra travel time, obey speed limits, and focus on safe driving rather than competing with other drivers.

question: What do "No passing zone" signs indicate?
options: a:To speed up slightly.,b:To maintain a steady speed.,c:That it is not safe to pass.
note: A "No Passing Zone" sign means you must not pass other vehicles in that area because it is unsafe, often due to limited visibility, hills, curves, or oncoming traffic risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Cross the centerline in an intersection.
note: You should never change lanes while you are in an intersection or by crossing the centerline there. Always wait until you are past the intersection, then signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and change lanes when it is safe.

question: What best describes distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,c:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
note: Distracted driving is anything that takes your attention away from driving, such as using a phone, eating, or adjusting controls. It reduces your ability to see and react to hazards and greatly increases crash risk.

question: Roads are most slippery at which moment during rainfall?
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,c:When they are clean and dry.
note: Roads are most slippery just after rain begins because oil, grease, and other residues that have built up on the dry pavement mix with the first water and rise to the surface. As rain continues, much of this residue is washed away and the road usually becomes less slippery.

question: Driving under the influence of medication that impairs your driving is:
options: a:Allowed if your physician prescribes it.,b:Under no circumstances permitted.,c:Allowed if you do not feel drowsy.
note: Driving is illegal any time you are impaired, regardless of whether the substance is alcohol, illegal drugs, or a prescribed medication. If a medicine makes you drowsy, dizzy, or slows your reactions, you must not drive, even if a doctor prescribed it or you feel you can handle it.

question: After a train passes and you have stopped at a railroad crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Drive around the lowered gates if it seems safe.,b:Proceed immediately since the first train has passed.,c:Wait for signals to stop flashing and look for a second train.
note: After a train passes, you must stay stopped until the warning lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised. Then look and listen carefully for another train on any track before crossing. Trains can come from either direction, and a second train may be approaching even after the first has passed.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as a vehicle's speed increases?
options: a:They increase.,b:They decrease.,c:They stay the same.
note: As speed increases, your stopping distance grows quickly and crash forces rise dramatically. This means you need more space to stop and any collision at higher speed will be more severe, so you should increase your following distance as your speed goes up.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake lightly to slow, then pull off safely.,b:Apply the brake and hold it down hard.,c:Pull over immediately without slowing gradually.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and ease off the accelerator. Avoid slamming on the brakes; brake gently only after you have the vehicle under control, then steer smoothly to a safe place off the road.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When another driver simply makes a mistake.,b:Whenever another vehicle is in your way.,c:When it may help prevent a collision.
note: Use your horn only when it may help prevent a collision or alert others to a hazard. Do not honk just because someone makes a minor mistake or is moving slower than you would like.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:When following a station wagon.,b:When following a driver who cannot see their vehicle's rear (like trucks),c:When following a small passenger car.
note: Leave extra following distance behind large vehicles like trucks and buses because they have large blind spots and limited rear visibility. More space also lets you see the road ahead and gives you more time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are large trucks likely to lose speed?
options: a:When driving down long hills.,b:When driving in long tunnels.,c:When driving up long or steep hills.
note: Large trucks usually lose speed when driving up long or steep hills because their heavy weight makes it harder to maintain speed while climbing. Expect them to slow down on upgrades and adjust your driving accordingly.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you get into the car.,b:Before you start driving.,c:Whenever you need to use them while driving.
note: Adjust your seat, mirrors, and safety belt before you start driving so you have a clear view and don’t need to make major adjustments while the vehicle is moving.

question: How should you drive on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement.,b:Your tires grip the road better than when you are driving on pavement.,c:Visibility is better than on pavement.
note: On gravel or dirt roads, your tires have less traction than on pavement, so it is easier to skid. Slow down, avoid sudden steering or braking, and allow extra distance to stop safely.

question: What can you do to reduce road rage incidents while driving?
options: a:Use your horn frequently.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Always signal your intentions when changing lanes.
note: Signaling early, driving courteously, and following traffic laws helps prevent misunderstandings and frustration that can lead to road rage. Letting others merge, avoiding aggressive gestures, and staying calm all reduce tension on the road.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you leaving little space, what should you do first?
options: a:Swerve into the adjacent lane.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal to create space.,c:Honk and step on the brake firmly.
note: When another driver cuts in front of you, the safest first response is to ease off the accelerator to increase your following distance smoothly. Avoid sudden swerving or hard braking unless absolutely necessary, as those actions can cause loss of control or a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, check the traffic, and go when it is safe to do so.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,c:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection without stopping.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way, then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

question: When roads are snowy or icy, how should you make speed and direction changes?
options: a:It is safe to use your cruise control.,b:Drive as you would under normal conditions.,c:Make changes more gradually than usual.
note: On snow or ice, traction is greatly reduced, so you must accelerate, brake, and steer more gradually than usual. Sudden changes can cause skids. Cruise control should not be used on slippery roads because it can cause the wheels to spin and you to lose control.

question: Before driving, remove snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:Just the windshield and passenger window.,b:All windows.,c:Just the windshield.
note: You must be able to see through all of your vehicle's windows and mirrors; remove all snow, ice, and frost before driving.

question: In traffic moving 50–55 mph, you are least likely to be involved in a crash if you:
options: a:Stay within that speed range.,b:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.,c:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
note: On high‑speed roads, you are safest when you travel at the same speed as surrounding traffic, as long as you are within the posted speed limit and driving at a speed that is safe for conditions. Large speed differences—either faster or slower than the flow—force more lane changes and passing, which increases the risk of collisions.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct action?
options: a:Turn sharply back onto the roadway immediately.,b:Stop where you are.,c:Reduce speed and re-enter the roadway gradually when safe.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, stay straight, and ease off the accelerator to slow down. Do not jerk the wheel back onto the road. After you have slowed and checked for traffic, gently steer back onto the pavement when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway, what should you do on the acceleration lane?
options: a:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.,b:Check for cars, accelerate to match the speed of traffic, and merge when safe.,c:Stop at the end of the acceleration lane and wait for a large gap.
note: On an interstate entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to build up speed so you can match the speed of traffic on the highway. Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and adjust your speed to merge smoothly. Do not stop in the acceleration lane unless traffic or signals require it.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means what?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and prohibited for traffic on the side with the solid line. Drivers on the broken-line side may pass when it is safe and legal; drivers on the solid-line side must not cross the line to pass.

question: If poor weather reduces visibility, you should:
options: a:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Drive faster to get off the road quickly.
note: When visibility is reduced by weather, you should slow down and increase your following distance. The extra space gives you more time to see hazards and stop safely if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly or conditions worsen.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take some caffeine pills.,b:Take a break.,c:Try to fight it.
note: If you become tired while driving, stop at the first safe location to rest, nap, or change drivers. Caffeine is not a substitute for rest.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must slow down, be prepared to yield, and watch carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians in the intersection.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what should you expect?
options: a:They must always wait off the roadway.,b:They may cut through all lanes.,c:They may use the left lane to make the turn.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and duties as drivers. To make a left turn, a bicyclist may move into the left lane or left-turn lane and turn like a motor vehicle when it is safe, or may use a crosswalk-style two-stage turn where allowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a road without a curb, after setting the parking brake you should:
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,b:Keep your wheels facing straight.,c:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
note: When parking uphill without a curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic and off the roadway instead of rolling into the lane.

question: What does a pentagon-shaped sign normally indicate?
options: a:School zone or school crossing.,b:Stop sign.,c:Regulatory sign.
note: A pentagon-shaped (five-sided) sign is used for school zones and school crossings. It alerts drivers to the presence of children and the need to slow down and use extra caution.

question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem while driving, you should:
options: a:Signal and move into the slow lane.,b:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road as soon as safe.
note: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem while driving, signal, turn on your hazard lights, and carefully move off the road and out of traffic when it is safe. Stopping in a traffic lane is dangerous and should be avoided unless your vehicle is completely disabled.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,b:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,c:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
note: You must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if no crosswalk is present; stop and allow them to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Use rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.,b:Use only your rearview mirror.,c:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
note: When entering a freeway, use your mirrors and also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before merging. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors and allows you to merge smoothly and safely into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always do what?
options: a:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,b:Stop.,c:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, always look to the sides as well as ahead to see if pedestrians, cyclists, or trains may be entering your path. Never pass vehicles that are stopped at a crosswalk or intersection for no obvious reason; they may be yielding to someone you cannot see.

question: If the vehicle in front of you stops at a crosswalk, what must you do?
options: a:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,b:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.,c:Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed before proceeding.
note: If the vehicle in front of you stops at a crosswalk, you must also stop and wait until you are sure all pedestrians have safely crossed. Passing a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk is dangerous because pedestrians may be hidden from your view.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in heavy rain?
options: a:Put on cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Immediately move to the shoulder when it starts to rain.
note: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning, slow down in wet conditions. Lower speeds help your tires maintain contact with the road surface instead of riding up on a thin layer of water.

question: A double solid yellow centerline means:
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from your direction of travel.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means you must not cross the lines to pass from either direction. You may cross only when making a permitted left turn or entering/exiting a driveway, but not to overtake another vehicle.

question: What color and lettering do temporary work zone signs use?
options: a:Yellow background with blue writing.,b:Orange background with black writing.,c:Red background with green writing.
note: Temporary work zone and construction signs are orange with black letters or symbols. This color combination alerts drivers to road work and the need to slow down and use extra caution.

question: Sudden gusts of wind on highways:
options: a:Only cause visibility problems.,b:Only affect the movement of large vehicles.,c:Can cause problems for all vehicles.
note: Sudden gusts of wind can push any vehicle sideways, especially at highway speeds. Drivers of all vehicles should be prepared to steer smoothly and firmly when passing open areas, bridges, or large trucks where wind gusts are common.

question: Which headlights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help others see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,b:You never need to yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians.,c:You should yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Only turn when there is a safe gap and the way is clear.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking if possible.,c:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking, which can cause loss of control, then brake gently and pull off the road when it is safe.

question: When driving on a slippery surface like snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.,b:Maintain traction by following other vehicles closely.,c:Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
note: On snow or ice, use a low gear before going down steep hills to help control your speed with engine braking. Increase your following distance and brake gently; if you do not have ABS, you may need to pump the brakes lightly to avoid skidding.

question: Why should you use antifreeze washer fluid in cold climates?
options: a:Cold fluid can scratch your windshield.,b:It will keep the washer fluid from freezing.,c:Moisture can cause cold wiper blades to crack.
note: In cold climates, washer fluid with antifreeze keeps the fluid from freezing in the reservoir, lines, and on the windshield, so you can clear salt, slush, and dirt and maintain good visibility.

question: How should you drive under low-visibility conditions due to fog?
options: a:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights.
note: In fog, reduce your speed and use low beam headlights so the light aims down at the road instead of reflecting back at you. High beams can reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. If visibility becomes very poor, pull off the road to a safe place and wait for conditions to improve.

question: What can happen if you take prescription drugs while drinking alcohol?
options: a:It can make you unfit to drive.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:There will likely be no effect.
note: Mixing alcohol with prescription or over‑the‑counter drugs can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and affect judgment. This combination can make you unsafe and unfit to drive, even if you took the correct medication dose.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:No one.,b:Overtaking cars.,c:Oncoming cars.
note: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, as well as to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Only turn when it is safe and the way is clear.

question: When a school bus is stopped ahead with flashing red lights and its stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Come to a complete stop only until all the children have left the bus.,c:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This protects children who may be crossing the road.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides. Avoid driving beside them for long periods; instead, pass safely and promptly so the driver can see you and you have room to react.

question: What do rumble strips do?
options: a:Through vibration and sound,b:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that create vibration and noise when you drive over them. This alerts drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, such as a stop sign or work zone.

question: If you see pedestrians near the road, how should you proceed?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: When pedestrians are near the road, you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass them with extra caution. Sounding your horn or maintaining speed can startle pedestrians and increase the risk of a collision. Always give pedestrians plenty of space and time to cross or move safely.

question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, what should you assume about the other driver?
options: a:Assume the driver will let you pass if you signal.,b:Do not assume they will make room for you to return to your lane.,c:Assume they will maintain a constant speed.
note: When passing, never assume other drivers will slow down, move over, or leave space for you to return to your lane. You are responsible for making sure there is enough clear space ahead and behind before you pull out and before you move back. Always check mirrors, blind spots, and oncoming traffic carefully.

question: Before moving back into your original lane after passing, what should you see?
options: a:Flash your headlights.,b:Beep your horn.,c:Both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing another vehicle, do not move back into your original lane until you can see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space ahead of that vehicle to return safely without cutting them off or forcing them to brake suddenly.

question: Which vehicle type is required to stop at all railroad crossings?
options: a:A school bus.,b:A dairy truck.,c:A cattle truck.
note: School buses, many transit buses, and vehicles carrying hazardous materials are required by law to stop at all railroad crossings, even if no train is coming. They must stop, look, and listen for trains before proceeding to ensure the safety of their passengers and other road users.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Brake lightly to slow the vehicle immediately.,b:Brake abruptly to stop the slide.,c:Stay off the brakes and steer in the direction you want the front to go.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay off the brakes and off the accelerator. Look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, making smooth, gentle steering corrections. Braking hard can lock the wheels and make the skid worse, reducing your ability to control the vehicle.

question: If you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Drive to the right edge and slow down but stay moving.,c:Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.
note: On most U.S. roads, when an emergency vehicle approaches from behind with lights and siren on, you must yield the right‑of‑way by moving to the right edge of the road and stopping. This creates a clear path down the center of the roadway so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely. If you are in an intersection, continue through it, then pull over to the right and stop.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Stay off the brakes and wait to drift to a stop.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
note: With antilock brakes (ABS), you should press the brake pedal firmly and keep holding it down. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup and allow you to steer while braking, even on snow or ice. Do not pump the brakes yourself in a vehicle equipped with ABS.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, what should you avoid doing immediately?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,b:Tap or pump the brakes.,c:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
note: In a tire blowout, avoid slamming on the brakes. Hard, sudden braking can cause you to lose control, especially if a front tire fails. Instead, grip the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow down gradually, and then brake gently once you have control and your speed has dropped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are approaching an intersection at the posted speed and the signal turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Proceed through without caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,c:Speed up to beat the light.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution rather than braking hard and risking a rear‑end collision.

question: How can you help the driver behind you maintain a safe distance?
options: a:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c:Maintain a steady speed.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling early helps drivers behind you judge distance and adjust their following space. Sudden speed changes make it harder for them to keep a safe following distance and can increase the risk of rear‑end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:
options: a:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,b:Inconvenience drivers.,c:Keep traffic out of hazardous work areas.
note: Work zone barriers, cones, drums, and signs are there to separate traffic from workers and dangerous areas. They guide you safely through or around the work zone and keep vehicles out of hazardous areas to reduce crashes and protect road crews.

question: Which statements about driving speed are true?
options: a:Both of the following are true.,b:As your speed increases, the risk and severity of crashes increase.,c:As your speed increases, you must increase your following distance.
note: As your speed increases, crashes are more likely to cause serious injury or death, and you need more time and distance to see hazards and stop safely. That is why you must increase your following distance as your speed increases, so you have enough space to react and brake without hitting the vehicle ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're being passed repeatedly while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right when safe.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane roads, the right lane is generally for slower traffic, and the left lane is for passing. If you are in the center lane and other vehicles keep passing you, you are likely going slower than the flow of traffic. When it is safe, move to the lane on your right so faster traffic can pass on the left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving more slowly than the surrounding traffic is:
options: a:A good idea in all situations.,b:Appropriate if you do not know the speed limit.,c:Often a hazard because other drivers may try to pass unsafely.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous because other drivers may make sudden lane changes or risky passes to get around you. This can lead to rear-end collisions or side-swipe crashes. You should generally drive at the speed of traffic, up to the posted speed limit and adjusted for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to, but not away from, the curb.
note: Any time you move your vehicle into or out of a traffic lane, you must signal. When parking at a curb, signal as you pull toward the curb so others know you are slowing and moving over, and signal again when you leave the curb to re-enter traffic so other drivers can anticipate your movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may legally block an intersection:
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,c:During rush hour traffic.
note: You must never enter an intersection unless you are sure you can clear it completely, even with a green light. Stopping in the middle of an intersection and blocking cross traffic is illegal and unsafe because it interferes with traffic flow and can cause collisions.

question: Which behavior may identify someone as an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:The number of passengers in their car.,c:Tendency to drive slowly.
note: Aggressive drivers often show impatience and hostility through their driving, such as making sudden, unsafe lane changes, tailgating, or speeding. These behaviors increase crash risk. The number of passengers or simply driving slowly does not by itself indicate aggressive driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection and the light changes from green to steady yellow, you should:
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection.,c:Speed up to get through more quickly.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely. Stopping in the intersection blocks traffic, and speeding up aggressively can cause crashes.

question: In very foggy conditions, you should slow down and:
options: a:Use high beam headlights.,b:Use your low beam headlights.,c:Turn on your emergency flashers only.
note: In fog, always slow down and use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, reducing visibility. If your vehicle has fog lights, you may use them together with low beams for better visibility.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: When animals are near the road, reduce your speed and be prepared to stop. Animals can move suddenly into your path and often travel in groups. Swerving or speeding up can cause you to lose control or collide with another vehicle.

question: If your car starts to skid, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Apply the brakes lightly.,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly.
note: When your car starts to skid, you should stay off the brakes and steer gently in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. Braking hard or pumping the brakes rapidly can make the skid worse by reducing traction even more. In most modern cars with ABS, you should press the brake pedal firmly and steadily only if you must slow down, but never pump the brakes in a skid.

question: What does the term BAC refer to?
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: BAC stands for Blood Alcohol Concentration. It is the percentage of alcohol in a person’s bloodstream and is used by law enforcement to determine if a driver is legally impaired. Implied consent is a separate concept that means drivers agree to chemical testing (such as breath or blood tests) in exchange for the privilege of driving.

question: If you must park somewhere not usually used for parking, what must you ensure?
options: a:Park with your reverse lights on.,b:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: If you must park in a place that is not normally used for parking, you must make sure your vehicle can be clearly seen by drivers coming from any direction. Good visibility helps other road users detect your parked vehicle early and avoid sudden swerves or braking that could cause a collision.

question: In bad or inclement weather you should:
options: a:Drive in a low gear only.,b:Steer off the road immediately.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.
note: In bad weather such as rain, snow, or ice, you should steer, accelerate, and brake smoothly. Sudden or sharp movements can cause your tires to lose traction and lead to a skid. Gentle, gradual inputs help maintain control and give your tires the best chance to grip the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time from your right and left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs or signals. If another vehicle is on your right and you arrive together, let that driver proceed before you enter the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left.,b:The driver who arrived before you.,c:The driver across from your vehicle.
note: At a four-way stop, drivers proceed in the order they arrive. The first vehicle to stop is the first to go. If two or more vehicles arrive at different times, the one that arrived first has the right-of-way. If vehicles arrive at exactly the same time, then the vehicle on the right goes first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check for vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Use only the outside mirrors.,c:Look over your shoulder.
note: Mirrors do not show the areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle; these are blind spots. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check these blind spots, while also using your mirrors and signal.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams and impairs your vision at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Look straight ahead in your lane.,c:Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim high beams, the bright light can temporarily blind you. Do not look directly into the headlights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision to track the oncoming vehicle. This helps you stay in your lane while reducing glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,c:You have the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. If the other vehicle is on your left, that means you are on their right, so you may proceed first when it is safe.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian while an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.,b:Honk to get the pedestrian to move over.,c:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.
note: When you face both a pedestrian in your lane and an oncoming vehicle, you should not try to squeeze between them. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Once it is clear and safe, then pass the pedestrian, giving them plenty of space and reducing your speed.

question: If your car's suspension is worn, what problem can it cause?
options: a:Vehicle control problems and difficulty handling.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: A worn suspension makes the vehicle bounce, lean, and react poorly to bumps and turns. This reduces tire contact with the road and can cause loss of control, especially in emergency maneuvers or on curves.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow, what helps others see you?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn up instrument panel lights.,c:Turn on only your parking lights.
note: In reduced visibility such as dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, you should turn on your low‑beam headlights so others can see you. Parking lights alone are not enough and are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

question: A school bus is stopped ahead with red lights flashing in your lane. What must you do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights are flashing.,b:Stop and proceed when you think children have exited.,c:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to go. The only common exception is when you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical barrier.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Vision.,b:Judgment.,c:Balance.
note: Alcohol first affects the parts of the brain that control judgment, self‑control, and decision‑making. This means you may take risks or misjudge situations before you notice obvious problems with balance, coordination, or vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which lane should you be in before making a left turn from a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the center of the street.,b:The lane nearest the left curb.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: On a one‑way street, a left turn should start from the lane closest to the left curb. This positions you correctly for the turn and reduces conflicts with traffic going straight or turning right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When stopped at a red light that also displays a green arrow for your lane, you may proceed in the arrow's direction if:
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,c:You wait until the main light changes to green.
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal. If you are in the correct lane for that arrow and the intersection is clear, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow even though the main signal is red. Always yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection.

question: Which headlights should drivers use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, you should use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, which makes it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help other drivers see you without increasing glare.

question: When in a work zone, how should you manage your following distance?
options: a:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Follow the driver in front of you closely.
note: In work zones you must avoid tailgating and leave extra following distance. Traffic can slow or stop suddenly, and workers or equipment may enter your lane. A larger space cushion gives you more time to react and helps protect everyone in the work area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you judge before starting to pass?
options: a:Flash your headlights as you pass.,b:Sound your horn as you pass.,c:The distance to any oncoming vehicles.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, you must be sure there is enough clear distance ahead to complete the pass safely without interfering with oncoming traffic. Only start to pass when you can see that the opposing lane is clear far enough ahead and you can return to your lane without forcing anyone to slow or swerve.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, rain, or snow, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only.
note: When visibility is reduced by fog, rain, or snow, use low beam headlights. High beams can reflect off water droplets or snowflakes and cause glare, making it harder to see. Low beams provide better forward visibility and make your vehicle more visible to others.

question: If the road ahead is flooded, what should you do?
options: a:Not drive through the flooded area; turn around and seek another route.,b:Slam on the brakes.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: Never drive through a flooded roadway. Even shallow water can hide deep holes, debris, or washed‑out pavement, and moving water can quickly sweep a vehicle away. If you see water covering the road, turn around and find another route.

question: When driving at night, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Always use your high beams.
note: At night, visibility is reduced, so you should increase your following distance and avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights to reduce glare. Use high beams only when there is no oncoming traffic and you are not following another vehicle closely; do not use them all the time.

question: If you park uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Toward the side of the road (right).,c:Toward the center of the road (left).
note: When parking uphill on a two‑way road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the side of the road so that if the vehicle rolls, it will move away from traffic and toward the shoulder.

question: Which is a dangerous habit in work zones?
options: a:Only tailgating.,b:Only failing to watch for workers and equipment.,c:Both tailgating and failing to watch for workers and equipment.
note: In work zones, following too closely and failing to watch for workers, equipment, and changing traffic patterns are both dangerous. Leave extra space, slow down, and stay alert for workers and machinery entering or crossing the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians and oncoming vehicles that have the right-of-way.,b:All approaching vehicles regardless of direction.,c:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a Walk signal only.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians who are in the crosswalk or otherwise have the right‑of‑way. Do not start your turn until it is safe and the way is clear.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you anticipate?
options: a:Beep your horn to warn them.,b:That the child may act unpredictably — expect the unexpected.,c:Assume the child is in full control of the bicycle.
note: Children on bicycles can be very unpredictable. They may suddenly swerve, stop, or enter your lane without warning. You should slow down, give them extra space, and be prepared to stop. Do not rely on them to stay in control or react like an adult rider.

question: When a pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane is crossing, what must you do?
options: a:Yield only at corners.,b:Tell them where to cross.,c:Yield the right-of-way at all times.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is legally blind or visually impaired and must always be given the right‑of‑way. You must stop or yield whenever they are crossing or preparing to cross, and never try to direct them or force them to hurry.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.,c:Only when a crossing guard is present.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog, whether they are in a crosswalk, at an intersection, or entering the roadway. Treat them as having the right‑of‑way at all times and be prepared to stop well in advance.

question: What is the only proven method to remove alcohol or drug combinations from your system?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Breathe fresh air.,c:Give your body time.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and remove alcohol or impairing drugs; other measures do not lower BAC.

question: If you become tired while driving you should:
options: a:Open a window for fresh air and continue driving.,b:Stop and either rest or change drivers.,c:Drink something with caffeine and continue driving.
note: If you feel tired while driving, you are at risk of drowsy driving, which is as dangerous as drunk driving. The safe action is to pull over in a safe place and rest or switch drivers. Opening windows or drinking caffeine cannot reliably keep you alert enough to drive safely.

question: From top to bottom, what is the standard vertical order of traffic lights?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:Yellow
note: Standard vertical traffic signals are arranged red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom so drivers can recognize the signal order even if colors are hard to see.

question: What do double solid yellow centerline markings indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Wait for the green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down, look carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop unless needed for safety.

question: Which habit blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene (rubbernecking).,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: Slowing down to look at a crash or roadside incident, called rubbernecking, disrupts the smooth flow of traffic and can cause additional collisions. Keep your attention on the road ahead and maintain a steady speed if it is safe.

question: If an accident causes over $500 in damage, when must you report it?
options: a:Immediately, regardless of who caused it.,b:Only if there are injuries.,c:Only if you are uninsured.
note: Any accident on a public highway that results in $500 or more in property damage must be reported by the driver involved, regardless of fault.

question: When you encounter a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, what must you do?
options: a:Honk your horn as you proceed.,b:Carefully drive around them.,c:Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.
note: A person using a white cane or guide dog is blind and has the right‑of‑way. You must stop and remain stopped until the pedestrian has safely crossed and is well clear of your path. Do not honk or try to drive around them, as this can be dangerous and confusing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you obey the instructions of a school crossing guard?
options: a:Only during school hours.,b:Unless you do not see any children present.,c:At all times.
note: You must always obey a school crossing guard’s instructions. They are authorized to direct traffic and protect children and other pedestrians near schools, and their directions must be followed whenever they are on duty.

question: When traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic if possible.,b:Always maintain your position regardless of circumstances.,c:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up.
note: When traffic is merging into your lane, help keep traffic flowing smoothly by adjusting your speed or lane position, when safe, to create space for merging vehicles. Do not speed up or block them; cooperation reduces collisions and sudden braking.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas around your vehicle that cannot be seen in the mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see using your mirrors alone, usually along the sides and near the rear corners. To check them, quickly glance over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you permitted to pass another vehicle on the road?
options: a:When a solid line is next to your lane.,b:On a hill or curve.,c:When a broken center line is next to your lane.
note: You may pass another vehicle only when a broken yellow center line is next to your lane and it is safe to do so. Do not pass when there is a solid yellow line next to your lane, or on hills, curves, or any place where you cannot see far enough ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,b:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it has passed.,c:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using flashing lights and/or a siren, you must move to the right side of the road and stop, clear of any intersection, and remain stopped until the vehicle has passed. This allows emergency responders a clear, predictable path and reduces the risk of collisions.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what should you do regarding safety belts?
options: a:Buckle only if you are driving on the highway.,b:Check passengers' belts after starting the car.,c:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers have buckled theirs.
note: Make a habit of fastening your belt and confirming others have buckled before starting the engine.

question: If you are under 21, your license may be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any amount.
note: Delaware enforces zero tolerance for drivers under 21: detection of any alcohol can lead to penalties including license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to turn left on a red light after stopping?
options: a:Whenever you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.,b:When you are on a two-way street turning onto another two-way street.,c:When you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street and no sign prohibits it.
note: In many states, you may turn left on a red light only when you are turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after coming to a complete stop, yielding to pedestrians and traffic, and only if there is no sign prohibiting a left turn on red. You may not turn left on red from a two-way street.

question: Which action should you never take when changing lanes?
options: a:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,c:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
note: You should never change lanes abruptly or without planning. Safe lane changes require signaling in advance, checking your mirrors, and looking over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving. A quick, sudden lane change increases the risk of sideswipe and rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers making a left turn must yield to:
options: a:No specific vehicles.,b:Passing cars only.,c:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
note: When you turn left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, including cars, motorcycles, and bicycles. You may only turn when there is a safe gap and you will not force oncoming traffic to slow or stop.

question: How should you change lanes from one lane to another?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:Gradually and carefully.,c:When a car is in your blind spot.
note: Change lanes only when necessary, after checking mirrors and blind spots, signaling, and making sure the lane is clear. Move over gradually and smoothly; never change lanes when a vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than daytime driving?
options: a:Your reaction time is slower at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:You cannot see as far ahead at night.
note: Night driving is more dangerous mainly because you cannot see as far ahead. Headlights provide limited range, and glare and darkness reduce how well you can see hazards, making it harder to spot problems in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red signal, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and enter with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped while the light is red.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way. Proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

question: What does a pennant-shaped yellow sign indicate?
options: a:Right turns permitted.,b:Right turns only.,c:No passing zone.
note: A yellow pennant-shaped sign, placed on the left side of the road, marks the beginning of a no passing zone. It warns you not to start passing other vehicles in that area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection showing a steady yellow light and you have not entered the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,b:Come to a safe stop.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should slow down and come to a safe stop, rather than speeding up to get through. Only continue through if you are already in the intersection or cannot safely stop in time.

question: If you are involved in an accident that causes injury, when must you report it?
options: a:Immediately.,b:Within 24 hours.,c:Within one week.
note: Any crash involving injury or death must be reported to law enforcement without delay. You are required to stop, remain at the scene, give required information, and notify the police immediately, not hours or days later.

question: A distraction while driving is:
options: a:Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from the driving task—your eyes from the road, your mind from driving, or your hands from the wheel. Examples include texting, eating, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers instead of traffic.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge of the road.,c:Grip the steering wheel firmly
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly to maintain control, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Do not brake hard. Once you have control and your speed has dropped, steer to a safe place off the road and brake gently if needed.

question: An orange and red triangular sign displayed on the back of a vehicle means:
options: a:Shoulder work ahead.,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:Slow-moving vehicle.
note: An orange and red triangular emblem on the rear of a vehicle indicates a slow‑moving vehicle, typically traveling 25 mph or less. When you see this sign, reduce speed, be prepared to slow further, and pass only when it is safe and legal.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Only to check for vehicles in blind spots.,b:Only when slowing down.,c:Often to monitor how traffic is moving behind you.
note: You should check your mirrors frequently so you always know what is happening behind and beside you. This helps you react early to vehicles that may be approaching quickly, changing lanes, or following too closely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop while the traffic light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the traffic signal.,b:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,c:Obey the police officer.
note: You must always obey the lawful instructions of a police officer directing traffic, even if their directions are different from traffic lights, signs, or pavement markings. The officer’s directions temporarily override normal traffic controls to keep everyone safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle:
options: a:If the shoulder is wide enough.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
note: You must not drive onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle. The shoulder is for emergencies and stopped vehicles, and other drivers do not expect moving traffic there, which makes passing on the shoulder very dangerous and generally illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light that shows a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction when:
options: a:You must first come to a complete stop.,b:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,c:You must wait until the light changes.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow. If you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear of pedestrians and other traffic, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow, even if other parts of the signal are red.

question: When a vehicle with bright headlights approaches at night, where should you look?
options: a:Look directly at the headlights.,b:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Stop in your lane until the vehicle passes.
note: When an oncoming vehicle’s bright headlights shine at you, do not look directly into them. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This reduces glare and helps you stay in your lane while still watching the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to block the pass.,b:Brake hard to prevent the pass.,c:Maintain a steady speed and allow the passing vehicle to complete the maneuver.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, stay in your lane and keep a steady speed, or slow slightly if needed. This makes it easier and safer for the other driver to pass and return to the lane without sudden speed changes or conflicts.

question: Your car may begin to hydroplane at speeds as low as:
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:40 miles per hour.,c:35 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. This can begin around 35 mph in standing water, and the risk increases as your speed goes up and tire tread or inflation are poor.

question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Pass the work zone carefully, obey posted work zone speeds, and avoid slowing down just to look at the scene.,b:Stop to watch the workers.,c:Reduce your following distance so you are closer to the vehicle ahead.
note: In construction zones, you should drive with extra caution, obey reduced speed limits, and avoid rubbernecking or unnecessary slowing that can cause crashes. Maintain a safe following distance—do not reduce it—so you have time to react to workers, equipment, or sudden stops.

question: Where are truck blind spots located?
options: a:On both sides of the truck, especially the immediate left of the cab, and directly behind the truck.,b:Directly behind the body only.,c:On the immediate left of the cab only.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots, often called “No-Zones,” directly behind the truck and along both sides, especially on the right side and close to the cab on the left. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, the driver likely cannot see you.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, you should:
options: a:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,b:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,c:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn.
note: Do not try to pass between a turning truck or bus and the curb; wait until the larger vehicle completes its turn.

question: Blue traffic signs provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services such as rest areas, food, or hospitals.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage information only.
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They guide drivers to motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals. They are not used for construction zones or general mileage information.

question: When finishing a passing maneuver, how can you tell you have enough room to return to your lane?
options: a:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,b:If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
note: After passing another vehicle, you should not move back into your original lane until you are sure you have enough space. A good rule is to wait until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed clearly in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have created a safe following distance before returning to the lane.

question: What can continuous hard braking on ice or snow cause?
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: On ice or snow, hard continuous braking can cause your wheels to lock. When the front wheels lock, you lose steering control and the vehicle may skid straight ahead. To maintain control, slow down early and brake gently and gradually on slippery surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should yield your legal right-of-way:
options: a:Never,b:Often,c:Whenever it helps prevent a collision.
note: Even if you have the legal right-of-way, you must be prepared to yield to avoid a collision. Other drivers may make mistakes or break the rules. Yielding your right-of-way when it helps prevent a crash is an important part of defensive driving.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare. High beams reflect off the fog and back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Parking lights alone are not bright enough and do not help other drivers see you well.

question: How should drivers check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Only the left outside mirror.,c:Look over the left or right shoulder.
note: To safely change lanes, check your mirrors first, then quickly look over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward. This head check lets you see the blind spot that mirrors cannot show, helping you avoid vehicles hidden beside you.

question: You should increase the following distance between your vehicle and the one ahead when you are:
options: a:Driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.,b:Following a small passenger vehicle.,c:Being tailgated by another driver.
note: When another driver is following too closely, you should increase your following distance from the vehicle ahead. Extra space in front gives you more time to slow or stop smoothly, reducing the chance of being hit from behind if you must brake.

question: Which statement correctly describes having a driver's license?
options: a:It is a legal requirement that cannot be revoked.,b:It is a privilege,c:It is a right
note: Driving is not a guaranteed right; it is a privilege granted by the state. You must meet licensing requirements and obey traffic laws, and your license can be suspended or revoked if you violate those laws or drive unsafely.

question: If you damage a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Leave a note with your name, contact information, and an explanation of what happened, and follow any required reporting laws.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must stop, try to find the owner, and if you cannot, leave a clearly written note with your name, contact information, and an explanation of the accident in a secure place on the vehicle. In many states you are also required to report the collision to law enforcement as soon as possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors you should:
options: a:Glance over your shoulder into the lane you want to enter.,b:Never look over your right shoulder.,c:Always slow down in your lane.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move. This shoulder check lets you see the blind spot and confirm the lane is clear before you steer into it.

question: What is the only truly effective way to remove alcohol from your body?
options: a:Wait — time.,b:Drink strong coffee.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; nothing speeds up the process.

question: On a slippery road, how should your following distance compare to normal?
options: a:Increase the distance from the vehicle ahead.,b:Keep the same distance as normal.,c:Follow more closely than usual.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction, so it takes much longer to stop. Increasing your following distance gives you more space and time to brake gently and avoid skidding or rear‑ending the vehicle ahead.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.,c:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and can often stop more quickly than larger vehicles. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or space to react if the motorcyclist brakes suddenly, increasing the risk of a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you face a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection, you must:
